name: Buran
tagline: Soviet shuttle; one unmanned flight, never crewed
dispatch: Buran was the Soviet Union's answer to the Space Shuttle — outwardly almost identical, but with two decisions that arguably bettered the original: it carried no main engines (all the lift came from the separate Energia rocket), and it could fly with no one aboard. On 15 November 1988 it proved the second, flying a complete uncrewed orbital mission and landing itself on a runway in a crosswind, something no winged spacecraft had ever done. It was a flawless flight and its only one. The Soviet Union collapsed, the money and the mission vanished, and Buran was cancelled — the flown orbiter later crushed when its hangar roof fell in 2002. One of the most impressive and most pointless achievements in spaceflight.
description: The Soviet shuttle, externally similar to the American orbiter but with no main engines (Energia carried it). Flew exactly once, in 1988, fully autonomous and unmanned — the only Soviet shuttle to ever reach orbit before the program ended.
best_known_for: Soviet shuttle; one unmanned flight, never crewed
